name: Congenital Patella Dislocation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Patella Dislocation

criteria.description: Irreducible lateral displacement of the patella present at birth
Radiographic evidence of laterally displaced patella on knee imaging
Presence of associated knee joint contractures or valgus deformity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of irreducible lateral patellar dislocation at birth confirmed by radiographic imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may be considered if syndromic features present

imaging: Lateral displacement of the patella on knee X-ray
Ultrasound showing absence of patellar tracking in trochlear groove
MRI demonstrating soft tissue abnormalities around the patella
genetic: Possible mutations in genes related to connective tissue and musculoskeletal development (e.g., TBX4, but no specific gene universally identified)
other: Clinical observation of fixed lateral patellar dislocation
Physical exam showing valgus deformity and limited knee extension

distinguishingFeatures: Onset in childhood or adolescence rather than at birth
May have patellar dislocation but accompanied by widespread joint involvement
Presence of muscle fibrosis and other systemic features

redFlags: Irreducible patellar dislocation causing severe functional impairment
Progressive knee valgus deformity leading to gait abnormalities
Delayed motor development due to musculoskeletal deformity
references: Bauer, J., et al. (2018). Congenital dislocation of the patella: diagnosis and treatment. Journal of Pediatric Orthopedics.
Smith, T. et al. (2020). Imaging features of congenital patellar dislocation. Radiographics.
